findings.location: Paragraph: “My husband faced the disaster like a man,” (English) -> “My man het die ramp soos ’n man aangespreek,” (Afrikaans)
findings.source_quote: “My husband faced the disaster like a man,” says Becky.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more idiomatic Afrikaans verb for 'faced' in this context, e.g. “My man het die ramp soos ’n man aangegaan” or “deurstaan” to convey the sense of confronting/enduring the disaster.
findings.translation_quote: “My man het die ramp soos ’n man aangespreek,” sê Becky.

findings.location: Paragraph about being asked to fill the food-committee role
findings.source_quote: Then I was asked to fill the position of food committee for Mrs. ‘Going-to-Bulgaria.’
findings.suggested_fix: The translation renders the role imprecisely as “pos van voedselaanbieder,” which reads as 'food provider' rather than a committee position. Use wording that preserves the committee/position sense, e.g. “om die pos op die voedselaanbodkomitee te vervul” or “om op die voedselkomitee te dien.”
findings.translation_quote: Toe word ek gevra om die pos van voedselaanbieder te vul vir mev. ‘Gaan-na-Bulgarye.’

findings.source_quote: Ocean waves breaking along a sandy shoreline seen from above.
findings.suggested_fix: The Afrikaans alt text uses “Oseaanwaaiers” (literally 'ocean fans'), which is incorrect. Use “Oseaangolwe wat langs ’n sandstrand breek, gesien van bo af.”
findings.translation_quote: alt="Oseaanwaaiers wat langs ’n sandstrand breek, gesien van bo af."
